newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY REPO CUT EXPECTED, MORE SEEN - TRADERS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY REPO CUT EXPECTED, MORE SEEN - TRADERS.

text.p: A 25 basis points repo rate cut by the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) on a working Saturday did not catch the market off-guard and traders said further cuts are likely within the next months.
"It did not come as a great surprise," said Adam Szilagyi of ABN AMRO Bank.
He added that he expects a further slow, but steady decline in repo rates over the next months.
"We could see one or two further cuts of a similar size," he said.
Another trader said she expected today's move to come a little later but that the cut was justified.

"Rates (on the inter-bank money market) usually hovered below the central bank's one-week reverse repo rate and there is no reason why the central bank should pay more than that," said Judit Kecskes of OTP Bank.

The NBH cut earlier on Saturday the overnight and one-week repo rates to 26.75 percent each, down 0.25 percent, the overnight reverse repo rate to 17.25 percent from 17.50 percent, the one-week reverse repo rate to 20.75 percent from 21 percent and the one-month reverse repo to 21.25 percent from 21.50 percent, effective immediately.
One trader said that with the six and 12-month deposit rates left unchanged at 21 percent and 20.50 percent respectively, the NBH was moving towards a more level interest curve.
"This move will somewhat iron out the (interest rate) differences which so far encouraged players to use the shorter-term repo facilities," said Balazs Benczedi of West-LB Hungaria.
